Definition: An enforceable constraint that agents, tooling, code, governance documents, human processes, and release operations must respect.
The governed root holding instruction-root resources; separate from and must not contain the working root.
The only ordinary location where agents may write project truth; must not be inside the instruction root.
Register mapping product-critical safety, audit, filesystem, lifecycle, transcript, settings, subagent, and human-gate boundaries.
The persisted, richer, versioned Chirality runtime event contract, distinct from browser UIEvent.
The stable, compact browser event contract, separate from persisted HarnessEvent.
The Chirality-owned runtime engine contract; provider/SDK APIs do not define public harness semantics.
The first concrete adapter and current shipped path; an implementation substrate behind Chirality adapters, not product identity.
A non-delegable approval point requiring accountable human evidence (e.g., CHECKING, ISSUED, domain-operation acceptance).
The canonical human-readable lifecycle state file for each deliverable; no other file determines deliverable state.
Record required, with explicit human acceptance, before a domain operation is applied.
A task agent whose execution requires sealed context, gate approval metadata, and inputs limited to folder contents and declared references.
A transport, not a permission bypass; in-process Chirality MCP tools obey the same permission, hook, path, redaction, and event policy as SDK built-ins.
